findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate the certified-op-routing prose so it states that verify.require_environment/opcert_enforce_since make only the completion-verifier lane enforcing (plan-review certs are verified via their own gate, not this toggle), matching verify_opcert.py's single KIND.

findings.finding: The plan states the MCP server signs 'plan-review + completion op-certs' and that such a cert 'becomes ENFORCING ... when verify.require_environment is set,' but the verify-opcert merge-gate enforces ONLY the completion-verifier kind; plan-review op-certs have no enforcement lane driven by require_environment/opcert_enforce_since (they are gated separately, e.g. the Gerrit bugfix-size gate). findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the Copilot static-bearer config to the exact retrieved config-file schema (`mcpServers.<name>.requestInit.headers.Authorization` in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, vs the `copilot mcp add --header` CLI form) and record the retrieved citation in the ADR rather than the ambiguous bare `headers` field.
evidence: Plan text: 'Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` `headers`) and Codex ... static-bearer-over-HTTP are verified against those tools' current official docs'
Retrieved GitHub Docs (Enterprise MCP config): `{ "servers": { "github": { "url": ..., "requestInit": { "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT" } } } } }`

Retrieved: Copilot CLI file `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` uses an `mcpServers` key; the `--header "Authorization: Bearer ..."` form is the CLI `copilot mcp add` flag, not necessarily the raw config-file key
The static-bearer capability itself IS corroborated for all three clients; the gap is only the exact config-file field name the olm slice will write
findings.finding: The plan asserts Copilot's static-bearer config uses a `headers` field in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, but current GitHub Copilot docs show remote HTTP MCP servers nest auth headers under `requestInit.headers` within an `mcpServers` entry (the bare header form is the `copilot mcp add --header` CLI flag). This capability assertion is under-precise about the exact config-file key.
scenarios: The olm client-config slice writes `headers` verbatim into `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and Copilot fails to attach the Authorization header because the key is actually `requestInit.headers`
The jackal live 3-client verification fails for Copilot on a config-schema mismatch discoverable now
findings.suggested_fix: In the ADR's recorded citations, replace the bare `headers` reference with the exact Copilot config-file key from current GitHub Docs (headers nested under `requestInit` inside an `mcpServers` entry), and note whether olm will use the CLI `copilot mcp add --header` form or hand-write the JSON.
